chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who bought a sacrificial animal for his mutʿah, then brought it to his منزل and tied it, but it got loose and perished. Does it suffice for him, or must he repeat it? He عليه السلام said: It does not suffice him, unless he had no power over it.

key_terms.عَلَيْهِ: over it or with respect to it
key_terms.فَانْحَلَّ: it came loose after being tied
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial animal designated for offering in hajj
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices or fulfills the obligation for him
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he must repeat or replace it

ai.seo_question: If a hady animal for tamattuʿ is lost or dies before reaching its place, does it still count?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sacrificial animal for tamattuʿ in hajj. If a person buys the hady and it is lost or dies before reaching its proper place, it does not suffice, and he must replace it, unless he had no ability or control over preventing that loss.
